prerequisites.title: Developer account with Owner role
prerequisites.detail: Only an owner can edit account settings and accept the Clover Developer Agreement.

prerequisites.title: Identity and business documents
prerequisites.detail: Have a passport or driver's license and proof of home address ready. Companies also need proof of business address and EIN/tax ID.

prerequisites.title: Two separate developer accounts
prerequisites.detail: Clover requires separate sandbox and production developer accounts.

steps.title: Create Clover Developer Account
steps.detail: Create a global developer account and enter developer info in Developer Settings.

steps.title: Submit account for verification
steps.detail: Click Verify Your Account, which also agrees to the App Market Developer Terms. Upload requested documents to Clover Box within 10 business days.

steps.title: Wait for account verification
steps.detail: Clover checks identity and runs an OFAC check. No duration is documented.

steps.title: Create production app and set OAuth URL
steps.detail: Create the app in the production dashboard, set the Site URL and OAuth response to Code, and request permissions.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your Clover client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Prepare listing and demo materials
steps.detail: Draft the use case description, listing text and demo script; check that production settings replace sandbox ones.

steps.title: Record video and submit app
steps.detail: Record the functional video, enter the use case and URL, then submit.

steps.title: Wait for App Market review
steps.detail: Chase Developer Relations if the review runs long.

traps.title: Sandbox settings left in production
traps.detail: Most functional failures come from leaving the environment on Sandbox or a broken redirect link.

traps.title: Silent rejections
traps.detail: A denied app may get no explanation; reply to the rejection email thread to get the reason.

traps.title: Documents deadline
traps.detail: Send requested documents within 10 business days or the application may be rejected. Never email identity documents; use Clover Box.

blockers.symptom: Review pending for a long time with no reply
blockers.what_it_means: Clover documents no review time, and a developer reported about 7 weeks of silence.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact Clover Developer Relations for a status update.

evidence.answer: For the Clover App Market, all submitted apps are reviewed before they can be listed, so this review applies to every app submitted (not conditional on scopes or user counts).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once your app is submitted, the Approval Status in the My Apps section and all other pages for your app display a Pending status.
evidence.answer: After submission, the app's approval status shows Pending while it is under review.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All apps submitted to the Clover App Market are reviewed to make sure they perform as expected, are free of bugs, and add value for merchants.
evidence.answer: The App Market review checks that the app performs as expected, is free of bugs, and adds value for merchants.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The team reviews the functional video and description you provide.
evidence.answer: The developer must provide a functional video showing a detailed workflow of the app, which the team reviews along with the description.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The video should help the Clover App Market team visualize your app's functional flow and how it benefits the merchant.
evidence.answer: The functional video should help the review team see the app's functional flow and how it benefits the merchant.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: describe the primary use case of your app, and click Save
evidence.answer: The developer must describe the app's primary use case in a functional description, and enter a URL to a functional use case video.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Create an app in the production environment
evidence.answer: The app must first be created in the production environment, selecting a subscription country where it will process payments.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click the Sandbox toggle icon to go to the production environment.
evidence.answer: To reach the production app pages, click the Sandbox toggle icon on the Global Developer Dashboard, then open the app under My Apps (this is for App Market submission, not OAuth client setup).

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Create a production developer account as described in Developer account approval .
evidence.answer: Creating the app for a production device requires a production developer account, which the page says must be created as described in Developer account approval.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: To integrate your point of sale (POS) with a production Clover device, you need to create a Clover app that merchants can install.
evidence.answer: The page's instructions cover creating a Clover app for integrating a POS with a production Clover device, so the app must be created to let merchants install it.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: External POS apps using the REST Pay API are not available on the public Clover App market, but your Clover apps are visible to merchants using your integrated POS.
evidence.answer: External POS apps using the REST Pay API (the semi-integrated type this page covers) are not listed on the public Clover App market, but are visible to merchants using the integrated POS.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To complete a payment on the Clover device, you must authorize your app to read merchant data from a Clover device.
evidence.answer: For card-present transactions, the app must request READ permission for Merchant so it can read merchant data from a Clover device.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Select the READ checkbox for Merchant.
evidence.answer: For card-present transactions, the READ Merchant permission is selected on the Edit Requested Permissions page and paired with a reason text.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If your app lets merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens for card-not-present (CNP) transactions, you must also configure your app for the Ecommerce API.
evidence.answer: Optional card-not-present support (for apps that let merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens) requires configuring the app for the Ecommerce API, in addition to READ Merchant.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: In the Ecommerce section, select the Enable online payments checkbox.
evidence.answer: For card-not-present support, the developer enables the 'Enable online payments' checkbox in the Ecommerce section of Requested Permissions.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In the Site URL field, enter the link (URL) of the home page of your web app.
evidence.answer: The REST configuration requires a Site URL, which must be the link to the home page of the web app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: When you set a CORS domain URL, your web app can make calls to the Clover REST API without requiring an intermediate app server.
evidence.answer: An optional CORS Domain URL can be set when integrating with Cloud Pay Display, and it lets the web app call the Clover REST API without an intermediate app server.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Log in to Developer Dashboard .
evidence.answer: The app is created by logging in to the Developer Dashboard and clicking Create App.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Select one or more countries where you want to make your app available for Clover merchants.
evidence.answer: In the Create App window the developer enters an app name and selects one or more countries where the app will be available to Clover merchants.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The App Settings—App Type section displays a Remote App ID (RAID) that uniquely identifies your semi-integrated app.
evidence.answer: For a semi-integrated POS app, the App Type section must be set with the REST Clients section set to Web and the integration question answered Yes, which then produces a Remote App ID (RAID).

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Your app needs OAuth tokens to authenticate API calls. You must configure a URL for the OAuth flow:
evidence.answer: The app's OAuth token needs are met by configuring a URL for the OAuth flow in the REST Configuration page, where the Default OAuth Response is set to Code.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: When your merchant is authorized through OAuth 2.0, you receive an authorization code. This code is required for you to request an API token for your app permissions.
evidence.answer: With the Code OAuth response, the developer receives an authorization code when a merchant authorizes through OAuth 2.0, and this code is needed to request an API token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: To proxy the callback through your domain, set the authorized redirect URI in your OAuth app's settings to your own endpoint.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The example redirect URI on your own domain is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately sends a 302 redirect to Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect, and must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
evidence.answer: The proxy forwards the callback to Composio's callback URL at backend.composio.dev.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through backend.composio.dev so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits display the Composio redirect URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: Routing the redirect through your own domain is only needed if you want to hide Composio's domain.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: `backend.composio.dev` flashes during OAuth redirect-back
evidence.answer: The browser address bar can show backend.composio.dev flashing during the OAuth redirect-back; the fix listed is to proxy the redirect through your domain.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: Bring your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: Users can see 'Composio wants to access your account' on Google, GitHub, etc.; the listed fix is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: When you proxy the redirect, the redirect URI registered with the provider is your own endpoint on your domain.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so you do not need to register your own (general Composio statement, not specific to Clover).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see
evidence.answer: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: With a custom auth config, you provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: Managed apps show users the consent-screen text 'Composio wants to access your account' during OAuth.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio."
evidence.answer: In production, users should see your app name rather than Composio, and this is the most common reason to switch to your own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes for managed apps may not include everything you need, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users, so you may hit rate limits; your own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants (for example a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: You can white-label the Connect Link page with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: You do not have to choose one approach for all toolkits; you can use your own credentials for some toolkits and managed auth for others, with each toolkit getting its own auth config.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: You receive 70% of the amount that Clover collects from the merchant for an installed app.
evidence.answer: For paid apps, the developer receives 70% of the merchant's app fees, and Clover collects the charges from the merchant, so the merchant pays for the app and the developer is paid a share.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Every app must have a subscription, even if it is a free subscription.
evidence.answer: Every app needs a subscription entry in the billing setup, even a free one, so pricing configuration is required even for free apps.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: You need to add bank account details to your verified Clover developer account to receive disbursements from Clover.
evidence.answer: To receive payouts for paid apps, the developer must have a verified Clover developer account with bank account details added.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: if your app has been under review for an extended period, it's recommended to contact Clover Developer Relations directly for a status update
evidence.answer: Clover's own docs say timelines vary and that apps under review for an extended period should be chased with Developer Relations; no typical duration is given.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: I submitted my application to the Clover App Market 7 weeks ago and it has been radio silence.
evidence.answer: Developer report (LinkedIn post, undated, about 2 years old): an App Market submission with only permissions and no APK sat about 7 weeks with no response, and the developer said follow-up emails went unanswered.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Reply directly to the rejection email thread—this often prompts a response with the reason for denial.
evidence.answer: Per Clover's docs, a denied app may get no explanation, and replying to the denial email thread is the suggested way to get the reason.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: App functionality is one of the top reasons for app rejections.
evidence.answer: Clover developer advocate blog: the main rejection categories are Legal and Privacy, Market Listing, and App Testing (Functional), with functionality among the top causes; common blockers include leaving Sandbox settings in production code and broken redirect links.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Most errors occur because of not changing the environment — Sandbox versus Production — in the code, or a broken link in the redirect.
evidence.answer: Most functional failures found in Clover testing come from leaving the environment set to Sandbox instead of Production, or from a broken redirect link.

items.reason: Quote states Clover must verify and approve the production developer account before the app approval process starts.
Quote states all apps submitted to the Clover App Market are reviewed for performance, bugs, and merchant value.
Quote states that after submission the approval status shows Pending while under review.
Quote says Clover verifies individual and corporate information, but says nothing about an OFAC check on every developer.
Quote states account approval is not needed if the developer intends to use only the sandbox environment.
Quote gives valid unexpired passport or driver's license with date of birth, but says nothing about proof of home address.
Quote gives proof of EIN/tax ID as a government-issued document, but says nothing about proof of business address.
Quote states revisions to approved or published apps are subject to review because they may impact the Developer Terms.
Quote states that after account approval Clover repeats the OFAC check monthly.
Quote states documents must be provided within 10 business days of the email or the application may be rejected.
Quote states Clover will review the account and reach out again if additional information is needed.
Quote recommends contacting Developer Relations for status after an extended review; no typical duration is given in the quotes.
Quote states the team reviews the functional video and description the developer provides.
Quote says to describe the primary use case and click Save, but says nothing about entering a URL to a use case video.
Quote states identity documentation should not be shared by email.
Quotes describe provider verification and review of the developer account and app, not acceptance of the company as a partner before use.
Quotes show account approval and app review are required before the app approval process and submission, but do not state the review is always required in every case.
Quotes support account verification before app approval and app review after submission, but do not give the full ordered list, including the demo video step as a separate gate.
Quotes support verification of identity/corporate information and a review of performance and merchant value, but do not mention why data is needed or the listing.
Quotes state revisions to published apps are reviewed and the OFAC check repeats monthly after approval.
Quotes state an approved production developer account is required before app approval starts.
Quote states account approval is not needed if the developer intends to use only the sandbox environment.

Quotes support sandbox needing no approval and App Market apps needing account verification and review, and the 7-week report, but the statement's 'no documented time' is only loosely supported and the 7-week figure is a single user report, which the quotes do state.
